description: A younger son demands his inheritance, squanders it in wild living, then returns home repentant. His father runs to embrace him and throws a feast. The older brother is jealous. Jesus teaches about God's forgiveness and grace.
At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turns water into wine when the wedding runs out. This is his first miracle, revealing his glory and causing his disciples to believe in him.
A royal official begs Jesus to heal his son who is near death. Jesus simply says 'Go, your son will live.' The official believes and his son is healed on the way home.
Jesus heals a man who has been an invalid for 38 years at the Pool of Bethesda. Jesus tells him to get up, take his mat, and walk. This heals on the Sabbath causes controversy.

Jesus feeds five thousand men plus women and children with five loaves of barley bread and two small fish. After everyone eats, twelve baskets of fragments remain. This is the only miracle recorded in all four Gospels.

Jesus walks on the Sea of Galilee toward the disciples' boat during a storm. Peter steps out of the boat and walks toward Jesus but sinks when he sees the wind. Jesus saves him and they return to the boat.

topic: Healing the Woman with the Issue of Blood
description: A woman who has been bleeding for twelve years touches the edge of Jesus' cloak and is immediately healed. Jesus feels power leave him and says 'Daughter, your faith has healed you.'

A synagogue leader named Jairus begs Jesus to heal his dying daughter. On the way, messengers say she is dead. Jesus goes to her room, takes her hand, and says 'Talitha koum' (Little girl, I say to you, get up!). She rises.

topic: Healing the Blind Man at Bethsaida
description: Jesus heals a blind man at Bethsaida by putting saliva on his eyes and laying hands on him. The man's vision is restored gradually. This demonstrates Jesus' power over blindness.

Jesus makes mud with his saliva, puts it on a blind man's eyes, and tells him to wash in the Pool of Siloam. The man is healed. Religious leaders interrogate him and the man eventually worships Jesus.
Ten lepers cry out to Jesus for mercy. He tells them to show themselves to the priests. As they go, they are cleansed. Only one returns to thank Jesus, and he is a Samaritan. Jesus praises his faith.

Jesus casts demons out of a man who lived among tombs, wore no clothes, and could not be restrained. The demons beg to be sent into a herd of pigs. The pigs rush into the sea and drown. The man is found clothed and in his right mind.

topic: Casting Out the Legion of Demons
description: Jesus casts a legion of demons out of a man in the region of the Gerasenes. The demons enter a herd of pigs that rush into the Sea of Galilee. The delivered man becomes a witness for Jesus in the Decapolis.

A fierce storm threatens to sink the disciples' boat while Jesus sleeps. They wake him, and he rebukes the wind and waves, saying 'Quiet! Be still!' The storm stops. The disciples ask, 'Who is this that even the wind and waves obey him?'
Jesus feeds four thousand men plus women and children with seven loaves of bread and a few small fish. After everyone eats, seven baskets of fragments remain. This is a second feeding miracle.

Lazarus has been dead for four days when Jesus arrives at his tomb. Jesus commands 'Lazarus, come out!' Lazarus comes out still wrapped in burial clothes. This is the greatest sign of Jesus' power over death.

topic: Healing the Man with the Withered Hand
description: Jesus heals a man's shriveled hand on the Sabbath in the synagogue. The Pharisees watch to see if he will heal on the Sabbath. Jesus asks, 'Is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the Sabbath?' He heals the man.

A Roman centurion asks Jesus to heal his servant. The centurion says Jesus need only say the word, just as he gives orders to his soldiers. Jesus marvels at his faith and heals the servant from a distance.
Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law of a fever. She immediately gets up and begins serving them. This is one of many healing miracles Jesus performs.

Jesus heals ten lepers by sending them to show themselves to the priests. They are cleansed as they go. Only one returns to thank Jesus, and he is a Samaritan. Jesus praises his faith and tells him to go in peace.

Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. His appearance is transformed, his face shines like the sun, and his clothes become white as light. Moses and Elijah appear and talk with Jesus. A voice from heaven says, 'This is my beloved Son.'

On the third day after his crucifixion, Jesus rises from the dead. The stone is rolled away from his tomb. Angels announce his resurrection to the women. Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, the disciples, and others over 40 days before ascending to heaven.

Jesus is nailed to a cross at Golgotha (Calvary) between two criminals. He is mocked and crucified. At noon, darkness covers the land. Jesus cries out 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' He dies and the curtain of the temple tears in two.

Judas leads a crowd with swords and clubs to arrest Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane. Peter cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant. Jesus rebukes Peter and surrenders. He is taken to the high priest's house for trial.

Jesus is tried before the Sanhedrin, Pontius Pilate, Herod Antipas, and Pilate again. Despite finding no fault, Pilate yields to the crowd and sentences Jesus to be crucified. He washes his hands to declare innocence.

Jesus shares a final meal with his disciples before his death. He breaks bread and wine, establishing the Lord's Supper (Communion). He washes the disciples' feet. He predicts his betrayal by Judas and Peter's denial. He gives the new commandment to love one another.

Jesus takes Peter, James, and John to the Garden of Gethsemane. He is deeply distressed and prays, 'Father, if you are willing, take this cup from me; yet not my will, but yours be done.' An angel strengthens him. He sweats drops of blood.

Jesus delivers his most famous sermon on a mountainside. He teaches the Beatitudes, the Lord's Prayer, love for enemies, and how to store treasures in heaven. It is the essence of his ethical teaching and the standards of the kingdom of heaven.

Jesus teaches the Beatitudes in the Sermon on the Mount: Blessed are the poor in spirit, those who mourn, the meek, those who hunger for righteousness, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, and those persecuted for righteousness.

Jesus teaches his disciples to pray: 'Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.'
Jesus teaches: 'So in everything, do to others what you would have them do to you, for this sums up the Law and the Prophets.' This is the principle of treating others as you want to be treated.

After his resurrection, Jesus commands his disciples to go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything he has commanded. He promises to be with them always.

Jesus is asked which is the greatest commandment. He answers: 'Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind.' And the second is like it: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' All the Law and Prophets hang on these two commands.

topic: I Am the Light of the World
description: Jesus declares 'I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.' This is one of the seven 'I Am' statements of Jesus in the Gospel of John.
Jesus says 'I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.' He knows his sheep and they know him. This is one of the seven 'I Am' statements of Jesus.

topic: I Am the Bread of Life
description: Jesus says 'I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.' He is the spiritual sustenance that gives eternal life. This is one of the seven 'I Am' statements.

topic: I Am the Resurrection and the Life
description: Jesus declares 'I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die.' He says this before raising Lazarus from the dead. This is one of the seven 'I Am' statements.

topic: I Am the Way, Truth, and Life
description: Jesus says 'I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.' He is the only path to God the Father. This is one of the seven 'I Am' statements.
Jesus says 'I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener. I am the vine; you are the branches.' Those who remain in him will bear much fruit. This is one of the seven 'I Am' statements.
Jesus says 'I am the gate for the sheep. I am the gate; whoever enters through me will be saved.' He is the only way to salvation. This is one of the seven 'I Am' statements.

Jesus comes to John the Baptist to be baptized in the Jordan River. As he comes up from the water, the heavens are opened, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven says, 'This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.'

After his baptism, Jesus is led by the Spirit into the wilderness for 40 days. Satan tempts him three times: to turn stones to bread, to throw himself from the temple, and to worship Satan for the kingdoms of the world. Jesus resists each temptation with Scripture.

Jesus calls twelve men to be his disciples: Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot. He gives them authority to drive out demons and heal diseases.
Jesus calls Simon Peter, Andrew, James, and John to follow him. He says 'I will make you fishers of men.' They leave their nets and follow him immediately. This is the beginning of Jesus' ministry.

Jesus sees Matthew (Levi) sitting at the tax collector's booth and says 'Follow me.' Matthew gets up and follows him. Jesus later eats at Matthew's house with tax collectors and sinners. Jesus says 'It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.'

Saul, a Pharisee who persecutes Christians, is traveling to Damascus when a bright light from heaven blinds him. Jesus speaks to him: 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?' Saul becomes Paul, the greatest missionary and writer of the New Testament.

Saul (Paul) travels to Damascus with letters to arrest Christians. A light from heaven blinds him. Jesus speaks to him. Saul fasts for three days. Ananias is sent to restore his sight and baptize him. Saul begins preaching about Jesus.

Fifty days after Easter, the Holy Spirit descends on the disciples gathered in Jerusalem. They speak in other languages. Peter preaches and 3,000 people are baptized. This is the birth of the Christian church.

In the beginning, God creates the heavens and the earth. He speaks light into existence, creates the sky, separates land from water, makes plants, sun, moon, stars, animals, and finally creates mankind in his own image. He sees that it is very good.

God forms Adam from the dust of the ground and breathes life into him. He puts Adam in the Garden of Eden to work it. God says it is not good for man to be alone, so he creates Eve from Adam's rib as a helper. They are both naked and feel no shame.

God commands Adam not to eat from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. The serpent tempts Eve, who eats and gives the fruit to Adam. Their eyes are opened to their nakedness. God curses the serpent, the ground, and Adam and Eve, and banishes them from Eden.

God sees that wickedness is great on the earth and tells righteous Noah to build an ark. Noah builds the ark, brings his family and pairs of animals. The flood covers the earth for 40 days. After the flood, God sets a rainbow as a sign of his covenant never to destroy the earth by water again.

God sends a flood to cover the earth, destroying all life except Noah, his family, and the animals on the ark. The waters cover the mountains. After 40 days and 40 nights, the waters recede. Noah sends out a dove and receives an olive branch, signaling the earth is drying.

Humanity speaks one language and begins building a city with a tower that reaches to heaven. God confuses their language so they cannot understand each other and scatters them across the earth. The city is called Babel (Babylon).

God tells Abram (Abraham) to leave his country and go to a land he will show him. God promises to make him into a great nation, bless him, and make his name great. Abraham believes God and sets out on faith.
God tests Abraham by telling him to sacrifice his only son Isaac. Abraham obeys, but at the last moment, an angel stops him and a ram is provided instead. God reaffirms his covenant with Abraham.

Jacob's favorite son Joseph is sold into slavery by his jealous brothers. He interprets dreams for Pharaoh and rises to power in Egypt. During a famine, his brothers come seeking food. Joseph reveals his identity and forgives them. The family settles in Egypt.

Joseph's brothers are jealous of him and sell him to Midianite traders for 20 pieces of silver. They dip his coat in goat's blood and tell Jacob he was killed by a wild animal. Joseph is taken to Egypt.

Joseph is sold to Potiphar in Egypt but is falsely accused and thrown into prison. He interprets dreams for Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker. Two years later, Pharaoh has a dream and Joseph interprets it as seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine. Joseph is made second-in-command of Egypt.

After 400 years of slavery in Egypt, God raises up Moses to lead the Israelites to freedom. Through ten plagues, God judges Egypt. The final plague kills the firstborn. The Israelites leave in haste, but Pharaoh pursues them with his army.

Pharaoh's army pursues the Israelites to the Red Sea. Moses stretches out his hand and God parts the waters, creating a dry path. The Israelites cross safely. When the Egyptians follow, the waters close in and destroy them.

God sends ten plagues on Egypt to force Pharaoh to release the Israelites: water to blood, frogs, gnats, flies, livestock plague, boils, hail, locusts, darkness, and death of the firstborn. Each plague targets an Egyptian god.

God gives Moses the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai: no other gods, no idols, do not misuse God's name, keep the Sabbath, honor father and mother, do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not covet.

Moses is tending his father-in-law's flock when he sees a bush burning but not consumed. God speaks to him from the bush and tells him to go to Egypt to free the Israelites. Moses asks God's name and God says 'I AM WHO I AM.'

The Philistine giant Goliath challenges the Israelites. The young shepherd David accepts the challenge with five stones and a sling. He strikes Goliath in the forehead and kills him. The Philistines flee. David becomes a hero.

King David sees Bathsheba bathing and commits adultery with her. She becomes pregnant. David arranges for her husband Uriah to be killed in battle. The prophet Nathan confronts David. David repents, but the child dies.

God sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint one of Jesse's sons as the next king. Samuel sees the eldest son and thinks he must be the one, but God says, 'The Lord does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.' Jesse's youngest son David is anointed.

Samson, a Nazirite with supernatural strength, falls in love with Delilah. The Philistines bribe her to discover the secret of his strength. She learns it is in his hair and cuts it while he sleeps. The Philistines capture him, blind him, and put him in prison.

Samson is consecrated to God as a Nazirite from birth. He has supernatural strength and fights the Philistines, killing many with the jawbone of a donkey. His strength is a gift from God, tied to his Nazirite vow.

Daniel continues to pray to God despite a decree making it illegal. He is thrown into a den of lions, but God sends an angel to shut the lions' mouths. Daniel emerges unharmed. King Darius is amazed and issues a decree honoring Daniel's God.

topic: Daniel and the Writing on the Wall
description: During Belshazzar's feast, a mysterious hand writes on the wall: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN. Daniel interprets the writing: God has numbered Belshazzar's days, weighed him and found wanting, and his kingdom will be divided. That night Belshazzar is slain.

God tells Jonah to go to Nineveh, but Jonah flees in the opposite direction. A great storm threatens his ship. The sailors throw Jonah overboard. A great fish (whale) swallows him. After three days, Jonah prays and the fish vomits him onto dry land. He goes to Nineveh.

Job, a righteous man, loses everything: his children, health, and wealth. His friends insist he must have sinned. Job maintains his innocence and questions God. God speaks to Job from a whirlwind, revealing his sovereignty. Job is restored.

Three mysterious visitors appear at Abraham's tent. Abraham serves them a meal. They prophesy that Sarah will have a son within a year. Sarah laughs in disbelief. The visitors are angels, and one is the Lord. They reveal their plan to destroy Sodom.

God tells Abraham he will destroy Sodom and Gomorrah because of their great sin. Abraham bargains with God to spare the city if ten righteous people are found. None are found. Two angels rescue Lot and his family. Fire and brimstone destroy the cities.

After the flood, God makes a covenant with Noah never again to destroy the earth by water. He sets a rainbow in the sky as a sign of this promise. This is the Noahic covenant, God's promise to all humanity.

Jacob dreams of a ladder reaching from earth to heaven with angels ascending and descending. God stands above it and reaffirms the covenant with Jacob. Jacob wakes and names the place Bethel (House of God).

Jacob wrestles with a mysterious man (often understood as God or an angel) all night at Peniel. His hip is dislocated, but he refuses to let go until he receives a blessing. His name is changed to Israel (one who struggles with God).

Moses ascends Mount Sinai and receives the Ten Commandments on two tablets of stone. The people make a golden calf while he is gone. Moses breaks the tablets in anger and intercedes for the people. God gives new tablets.

In the wilderness, God provides manna (bread-like substance) from heaven each morning for the Israelites. On the sixth day they gather twice as much for the Sabbath. This tests their obedience and dependence on God.

The Israelites are thirsty in the wilderness. God tells Moses to strike the rock at Horeb. When he does, water flows out. Later at Meribah, God tells Moses to speak to the rock, but Moses strikes it again in anger. Moses is punished.

topic: Elijah and the Prophets of Baal
description: Elijah challenges 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. He offers a sacrifice and prays for fire from heaven. Fire falls and consumes the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the water. The people fall on their faces and proclaim the Lord is God.

During a drought, God sends ravens to bring bread and meat to Elijah by the Brook Cherith. Elijah drinks from the brook. After the brook dries up, God sends him to a widow in Zarephath who provides food.

Elijah and Elisha cross the Jordan River. A chariot of fire and horses of fire appear and separate them. Elijah is taken up to heaven in a whirlwind. Elisha picks up Elijah's cloak and strikes the Jordan, parting the waters.

A widow's creditors are coming to take her two sons as slaves. Elisha tells her to borrow jars and pour her small amount of oil into them. The oil keeps flowing until all jars are full. She sells the oil and pays her debts.

Naaman, commander of the Syrian army, has leprosy. Elisha tells him to wash seven times in the Jordan River. Naaman is angry but obeys and is healed. He offers gifts but Elisha refuses them. Naaman acknowledges the God of Israel.

Isaiah sees the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted, with seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy.' Isaiah says 'Woe to me! I am ruined!' A seraph touches his lips with a live coal and cleanses his guilt. God asks, 'Whom shall I send?' Isaiah answers, 'Here am I. Send me.'

Isaiah prophesies about the Suffering Servant who will be pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. By his wounds we are healed. This prophecy is understood as foretelling Jesus' death on the cross.
Isaiah prophesies that a virgin will conceive and give birth to a son and will call him Immanuel (God with us). This prophecy is fulfilled in the birth of Jesus Christ.

Isaiah prophesies that a child will be born to us, a son will be given to us, and the government will be on his shoulders. He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

Mary, a virgin, is told by the angel Gabriel she will conceive by the Holy Spirit. She gives birth to Jesus in Bethlehem because of a census. She wraps him in cloths and lays him in a manger because there is no room at the inn.

The angel Gabriel appears to Mary in Nazareth and tells her she will conceive and give birth to Jesus, the Son of God. Mary asks how this can be since she is a virgin. Gabriel says the Holy Spirit will come upon her. Mary responds, 'I am the Lord's servant.'
Wise men (Magi) from the East follow a star to Bethlehem to find the newborn king of the Jews. They bring gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh. They worship Jesus and present their treasures.

An angel warns Joseph in a dream that King Herod wants to kill Jesus. Joseph, Mary, and Jesus flee to Egypt. They remain there until Herod dies. This fulfills the prophecy, 'Out of Egypt I called my son.'
King Herod orders the execution of all boys in Bethlehem two years old and under, trying to kill the infant Jesus. This fulfills the prophecy of Jeremiah about Rachel weeping for her children.

topic: Jesus in the Temple at Twelve
description: At age twelve, Jesus travels to Jerusalem for Passover. His parents lose him and find him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, asking questions. He says, 'Didn't you know I had to be in my Father's house?'

At a wedding in Cana, when the wine runs out, Jesus turns six stone jars of water into wine. It is the best wine. This is his first miraculous sign and reveals his glory. His disciples believe in him.

Jesus enters the temple and drives out the money changers and merchants, overturning their tables. He declares, 'My house will be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers.' This shows his authority over the temple.

topic: Sermon on the Mount - Love Your Enemies
description: Jesus teaches to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you. If you love those who love you, what reward is there? Be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect. This turns conventional wisdom upside down.

topic: Sermon on the Mount - Do Not Worry
description: Jesus teaches not to worry about tomorrow, what you will eat or drink or wear. Look at the birds of the air and the lilies of the field. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Seek first his kingdom and his righteousness.

topic: Sermon on the Mount - Salt and Light
description: Jesus tells his disciples they are the salt of the earth and the light of the world. A city on a hill cannot be hidden. Let your light shine before others that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.

In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus comes to the disciples walking on the sea. Peter steps out of the boat to walk to Jesus but sinks when he sees the wind. Jesus saves him and says, 'You of little faith, why did you doubt?'

Jesus asks his disciples who people say he is. Peter answers, 'You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.' Jesus blesses Peter and says, 'On this rock I will build my church.' This is a turning point in Jesus' ministry.
As Jesus approaches Jerusalem, he weeps over the city and says, 'If you had known what would bring you peace — but now it is hidden from your eyes.' He foresees the destruction of Jerusalem.

Jesus arrives at the tomb of Lazarus, who has been dead four days. He weeps. Then he commands, 'Lazarus, come out!' Lazarus comes out still wrapped in burial clothes. Many Jews believe in Jesus because of this sign.

Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey. Crowds wave palm branches and shout 'Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!' They lay cloaks and branches on the road. This fulfills the prophecy of Zechariah.

Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve disciples, agrees to betray Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver. He identifies Jesus with a kiss in the Garden of Gethsemane. He later regrets his betrayal and hangs himself.

Peter follows Jesus after his arrest to the courtyard of the high priest. He denies knowing Jesus three times before the rooster crows. Jesus looks at Peter. Peter remembers Jesus' prophecy and weeps bitterly.

Jesus speaks seven last phrases from the cross: 'Father forgive them,' 'Today you will be with me in paradise,' 'Woman, behold your son,' 'My God, why have you forsaken me,' 'I thirst,' 'It is finished,' 'Father, into your hands I commit my spirit.'

Joseph of Arimathea, a member of the Sanhedrin who had not consented to Jesus' crucifixion, asks Pilate for Jesus' body. He wraps it in a clean linen cloth and places it in his own new tomb, carved out of rock. A large stone is rolled in front.

Forty days after his resurrection, Jesus leads the disciples to the Mount of Olives. He blesses them and is taken up into heaven. Two angels appear and say, 'This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go.'
Before ascending, Jesus promises the disciples that they will receive the Holy Spirit. He tells them to wait in Jerusalem until the Spirit comes. This promise is fulfilled at Pentecost.

Paul undertakes three missionary journeys across the Roman Empire, preaching the gospel, planting churches, and facing persecution. He travels through modern-day Turkey, Greece, and eventually to Rome. He writes letters to the churches he founded.

Paul is being transported to Rome as a prisoner when a great storm drives the ship off course. After 14 days at sea, the ship runs aground near Malta and breaks apart. All 276 people on board survive, fulfilling God's promise to Paul.

Paul is arrested in Jerusalem and brought before the Sanhedrin. He says he has lived his life with a clear conscience. The Pharisees and Sadducees argue about the resurrection. The dispute becomes violent and Paul is pulled away for safety.

On the road to Damascus, a bright light from heaven blinds Saul (Paul). Jesus speaks to him: 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?' Saul asks, 'Who are you, Lord?' Jesus says, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.' Saul is converted.

Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, preaches boldly before the Sanhedrin. He accuses them of resisting the Holy Spirit. They drag him outside and stone him. Stephen sees heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God. He prays, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them.'

Philip is told by an angel to go to the road where an Ethiopian official is reading Isaiah. Philip explains the Scripture and asks if he believes. The Ethiopian says, 'I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.' Philip baptizes him.

God sends a vision to Cornelius, a Roman centurion, and separately to Peter. Peter understands that God does not show favoritism. He goes to Cornelius' house and preaches. The Holy Spirit falls on all who hear. Gentiles receive the gospel.

Jesus heals the sick, the blind, the lame, and the demon-possessed throughout his ministry. He has compassion on the crowds and heals them all. These miracles demonstrate his authority over disease, demons, and death.

People bring their children to Jesus, but the disciples try to turn them away. Jesus says, 'Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.' He places his hands on them and blesses them.

topic: Jesus and the Rich Young Ruler
description: A rich young ruler asks Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life. Jesus says, 'Go, sell everything you have and give to the poor, and come, follow me.' The man goes away sad because he has great wealth. Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom.

Jesus meets a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well. He asks her for a drink and then tells her about living water. He reveals he knows about her five husbands. She recognizes him as the Messiah. This is a key moment of Jesus reaching out to Samaritans.

When Jesus sees Mary and the Jews weeping over Lazarus, he is deeply moved and troubled. He weeps. This is the shortest verse in the Bible: 'Jesus wept.' His tears show his deep love and compassion for his friends.

In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John and prays. He is deeply distressed and prays three times for the cup to be taken from him. An angel strengthens him. He sweats drops of blood. He submits to the Father's will.

Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. He is transfigured before them. His face shines like the sun and his clothes become white as light. Moses and Elijah appear and talk with Jesus. A voice from heaven says, 'Listen to him.'

topic: Jesus Heals the Centurion's Servant from a Distance
description: A centurion asks Jesus to heal his servant. Jesus is willing to go to his house, but the centurion says Jesus need only say the word. Jesus marvels at his faith and says, 'I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.' The servant is healed that hour.

A furious storm arises while Jesus and the disciples are in a boat. Jesus is sleeping. The disciples wake him, terrified. He rebukes the wind and the sea, saying 'Quiet! Be still!' The storm stops completely. Jesus asks, 'Why are you so afraid?'

Jesus has compassion on the crowd of four thousand people who have been with him three days. He takes seven loaves and a few small fish, gives thanks, breaks them, and the disciples distribute them. Seven baskets of fragments remain.

topic: Jesus Heals the Blind Man at Jericho
description: As Jesus leaves Jericho, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus cries out, 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' Jesus stops and asks, 'What do you want me to do for you?' The man says, 'Rabbi, I want to see.' Jesus says, 'Go, your faith has healed you.' Immediately he can see.

Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, is small and climbs a sycamore-fig tree to see Jesus pass by. Jesus stops and says, 'Zacchaeus, come down. I must stay at your house today.' Zacchaeus gladly welcomes him. He pledges to give half his possessions to the poor.

Jesus sits near the temple treasury watching people put money in. Many rich people put in large amounts. A poor widow puts in two small coins. Jesus says, 'Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all the others. She put in all she had to live on.'

Jesus curses a fig tree that has leaves but no fruit. The next day it has withered. Jesus uses this to teach about faith and hypocrisy. He says if you have faith and do not doubt, you can say to this mountain, 'Go, throw yourself into the sea,' and it will be done.

topic: Parable of the Wheat and the Tares
description: A man sows good seed in his field, but an enemy sows weeds among the wheat. The servants want to pull up the weeds, but the owner says to wait until harvest. At harvest time, the weeds are gathered and burned, and the wheat is stored. This teaches about final judgment.

Jesus teaches, 'I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit. Apart from me you can do nothing.' This is a key teaching about abiding in Christ and the importance of relationship with him.

In the upper room, Jesus prays for his disciples and for all future believers. He prays for their protection, sanctification, unity, and glorification. He prays that they may be one as he and the Father are one.

At the Last Supper, Jesus takes a basin and towel and washes the disciples' feet. He says, 'If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another's feet.' This is an example of humble service.

After the resurrection, two disciples walk from Jerusalem to Emmaus. Jesus walks with them but they don't recognize him. He explains the Scriptures concerning himself. When they break bread together, their eyes are opened and they recognize him. He disappears.

Thomas was absent when Jesus first appeared to the disciples. He doubts the resurrection. Jesus appears again and invites Thomas to touch his wounds. Thomas exclaims, 'My Lord and my God!' Jesus says, 'Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.'

Jesus leads the disciples to the Mount of Olives, blesses them, and is taken up into heaven. Two angels in white appear and say, 'This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen him go.'

topic: The Promise of the Holy Spirit
description: Jesus tells the disciples that the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, will come upon them and they will be his witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth. He promises the Spirit will teach them and remind them of everything he said.

A manager is accused of wasting his master's possessions. He reduces the debts of his master's debtors to make friends for himself after he is dismissed. The master commends him for his shrewdness. Jesus teaches about the wisdom of using worldly wealth for eternal purposes.

topic: Parable of the Pharisee and Tax Collector
description: Two men go up to the temple to pray. A Pharisee thanks God that he is not like other people. A tax collector beats his breast and says, 'God, have mercy on me, a sinner.' Jesus says the tax collector went home justified before God, not the Pharisee.

topic: Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus
description: A rich man lives in luxury while Lazarus, covered in sores, lies at his gate. Both die. Lazarus is carried to Abraham's bosom, but the rich man goes to hell. The rich man asks Abraham to send Lazarus to warn his brothers. Abraham says they have Moses and the Prophets.

A nobleman gives ten servants each a mina and tells them to put it to work. Some double their money, but one hides it. The nobleman rewards the faithful servants and punishes the one who did nothing. Jesus teaches about faithfulness with what God has given.
